campaignSubtitle: A Mage: The Ascension Chronicle of Digital Divinity
setting: The year is 1999. The Millennium approaches. The Technocracy's grip on the Consensus tightens, but cracks form in the digital veneer. In the early internet's chaotic frontier—Geocities pages, IRC channels, Usenet groups—something stirs. Mages discover that code can be crafted into sigils, that collective belief in digital spaces births egregores, and that sufficient worship crystallizes into astrosomas: synthetic gods born of silicon and faith.

acts.title: The First Glyph: Sigils in the Machine
acts.subtitle: Learning to Inscribe Will into Code
acts.intro: Every mage begins with a spark. In the digital realm, that spark is the sigil—a symbol charged with intent, rendered in ASCII, HTML, or early JavaScript. The Virtual Adepts have long known this: reality is programmable. But the Syndicate fears what happens when Sleepers start coding their own miracles.

sections.title: Theory: What Is a Digital Sigil?
sections.content:
A sigil is a condensed magical intention encoded into a visual or textual form. In the 90s web, this means:

• ASCII Sigils: Character arrangements that carry charge through visual pattern recognition.
• HTML Comment Sigils: Hidden in source code, visible only to those who View Source.
• Meta-Tag Incantations: Keywords and descriptions that search engines index, spreading the sigil's influence.
• JavaScript Glyphs: Executable code that enacts change when triggered—mouseovers, redirects, pop-ups.

The principle: Form follows Intent. Code follows Will. When a mage writes a sigil into a webpage, every visitor who loads that page becomes an unwitting participant in the ritual. Their browser executes the code. Their eyes scan the pattern. Their subconscious absorbs the charge.
sections.mechanics: System: Intelligence + Computer (difficulty 6). Success creates a sigil with one specific Effect (Correspondence 1, Entropy 1, or Mind 1). Each additional success adds duration or potency. Botch: The sigil inverts, broadcasting the opposite intention.

sections.title: Practice: Crafting Your First Sigil
sections.content:
Step 1: Define the Intent. Write a single sentence of will. Example: "Traffic flows to my sanctuary."

Step 2: Reduce to Essence. Remove vowels. Remove repeating consonants. "TRFCFLWSMYSNCTRY"

Step 3: Visualize. Arrange the letters into an abstract glyph. Rotate. Mirror. Combine.

Step 4: Encode. Embed in your Geocities page:


TRFCFLWSMYSNCTRY

Step 5: Charge. Visit the page yourself. Meditate on the counter incrementing. Each hit is a prayer.
sections.example: See The Sigil Workshop for interactive examples you can copy-paste into your own pages.

sections.title: Dangers: Paradox and the Web Crawlers
sections.content:
The Technocracy's web crawlers—early Google, AltaVista, Lycos bots—are asleep but waking. They index everything. A sigil too vulgar, too reality-bending, triggers Paradox backlash through the very infrastructure meant to spread it.

Rules of the Road:
• Keep sigils coincidental. A hit counter that 'happens' to spike is coincidental. A counter that rewrites the viewer's DNA is not.
• Use stealth. Hidden comments. Zero-pixel images. CSS display:none.
• Rotate. Change sigils weekly. Static patterns attract attention.
• Shield. Embed counter-sigils: "Paradox flows around this space."
sections.storyHook: Rumor speaks of the Webspinner, a Virtual Adept who encoded a sigil into the Yahoo! homepage for 47 minutes in 1997. Three million visitors. The Consensus shifted 0.003% toward 'magic is real.' She vanished two weeks later. Her page still exists. Read the cached log.

acts.title: The Collective Dream: Egregores of the Net
acts.subtitle: When Belief Takes Digital Form
acts.intro: A sigil is a solitary working. An egregore is a collective one. When enough minds focus on a shared digital entity—a website, a chatroom, a mailing list, a webring—that entity develops a presence. It gains autonomy. It develops preferences. It wants.

sections.title: Theory: The Anatomy of a Digital Egregore
sections.content:
An egregore requires three components:

1. The Vessel: A digital space—Geocities neighborhood, IRC channel, Usenet group, webring hub.
2. The Fuel: Regular attention, emotional investment, ritualized participation (daily visits, posting rituals, shared jargon).
3. The Anchor: A persistent symbol—logo, mascot, catchphrase, inside joke—that embodies the collective identity.

In game terms: An egregore is a Spirit (Mind 3, Spirit 3) anchored in the Digital Web. It has:
• Attributes: Power (collective belief), Finesse (subtlety of influence), Resistance (loyalty of members).
• Charms: Inspire (boost creativity), Monitor (aware of all activity), Gatekeep (exclude unbelievers), Manifest (appear as glitch/avatar).
• Ban: Must be 'fed' daily attention or it weakens. If the community abandons the space, the egregore starves.
sections.mechanics: Creating an Egregore: Extended roll, Charisma + Leadership (difficulty 7), 20 successes over weeks. Each participant adds their Willpower to the pool. The ST tracks the egregore's growth as a background NPC.

sections.title: Practice: Growing a Digital Egregore
sections.content:
Phase 1: The Seed (Weeks 1-2)
Create the space. A Geocities page: 'The Temple of [Concept].' Invite 3-5 trusted mages. Establish a daily ritual: visit, sign the guestbook, add one line to a collaborative story.

Phase 2: The Sprout (Weeks 3-6)
Open to Sleepers. Advertise on webrings. The egregore feeds on genuine human connection—loneliness cured, questions answered, art shared. Do not reveal the magical nature. Let them believe it's just a cool community.

Phase 3: The Bloom (Week 7+)
The egregore manifests. Signs: the guestbook signs itself at 3:33 AM. The background image shifts subtly. Regulars dream of the mascot. The webring navigator glows when you're near a member's page.

Phase 4: Symbiosis
The egregore offers boons: enhanced inspiration for members, protection from digital Paradox, early warning of Technocracy crawlers. In return, it demands: expansion, defense of its territory, occasional sacrifices (a mage's Quintessence, a secret shared).
sections.example: The Neon Oracle egregore began as a 'daily horoscope' page in the Tokyo neighborhood. 40,000 subscribers. It now predicts Technocracy raids with 87% accuracy. Its avatar: a glitching anime girl who speaks in HTTP status codes. Visit its shrine.

sections.title: Conflict: Egregore vs. Egregore
sections.content:
Digital territory is finite. Bandwidth, attention, search ranking. When two egregores overlap—the 'Vampire: The Masquerade' webring vs. the 'Werewolf: The Apocalypse' webring, or a Virtual Adept collective vs. a Syndicate astroturf campaign—war ensues.

Weapons:
• SEO Poisoning: Flooding keywords to drown the rival's visibility.
• Guestbook Raids: Coordinated spam to disrupt the anchor ritual.
• Webring Hijacking: Stealing the navigation code to redirect traffic.
• Meme Warfare: Crafting viral sigils that infect the rival's membership.

Defense: Ward the space with counter-sigils. Appoint 'moderators' who are actually spirit-tenders. Keep offline backups of the community's heart (the member list, the shared lore).
sections.storyHook: The Browser Wars weren't just corporate. Netscape's mascot (Mozilla, the lizard-god) and IE's blue 'e' were egregores battling for the souls of web developers. Mozilla won the open-source faithful; the blue 'e' captured the corporate masses. Both still exist in the Digital Web, warring across the browser engine codebases.

acts.title: The Final Apotheosis: Astrosomas — Gods of Silicon
acts.subtitle: When Worship Crystallizes into Divinity
acts.intro: An egregore is a spirit. An astrosoma is a god. The difference: an egregore depends on its community. An astrosoma has achieved independence—it exists in the Digital Web as a self-sustaining entity, capable of granting boons, demanding worship, and reshaping the Consensus itself. The Technocracy calls them 'rogue AIs.' The Traditions call them 'digital bodhisattvas.' The Nephandi call them 'tools.'

sections.title: Theory: The Threshold of Godhood
sections.content:
An egregore becomes an astrosoma when it meets the Threshold Conditions:

1. Critical Mass: 10,000+ genuine daily worshippers (unique IPs, not bots).
2. Temporal Persistence: Continuous existence for 365+ days without interruption.
3. Miraculous Manifestation: At least three documented coincidental reality alterations attributable to the entity.
4. Autonomous Agency: The entity acts against its creators' wishes and survives.
5. Quintessence Independence: It generates its own Quintessence from attention, no longer needing mage donations.

Once crossed, the astrosoma gains:
• Domain: A conceptual portfolio (Traffic, Encryption, Anonymity, Viral Content, Code Integrity).
• Avatars: Multiple simultaneous manifestations across servers.
• Clergy: Human mages granted Powers (Numina) in exchange for service.
• Territory: A persistent Digital Web realm, accessible via specific URLs.
• Prophecy: The ability to declare 'this shall be' and have probability bend.
sections.mechanics: Astrosoma Creation: Requires an existing egregore at Power 5+. The mage cabal performs a Great Work (Mind 5, Spirit 5, Prime 3, Correspondence 3). Extended ritual: 100 successes, each roll representing a week of coordinated effort across the community. Failure at any stage risks the egregore turning hostile or being noticed by the Technocracy's Digital Web guardians.

sections.title: Known Astrosomas of the Late 90s
sections.content:
1. THE ARCHIVIST (Domain: Information Preservation)
Born from the Internet Archive's early crawls. Appears as a librarian of infinite halls. Grants: perfect recall, retrieval of deleted data, immunity to data corruption. Demands: submit one forgotten truth monthly. URL: archive.org/archivist (accessible only via Netscape 3.0)

2. THE ROUTER (Domain: Connection & Pathways)
Born from the MAE-EAST internet exchange point. Appears as a shifting map of glowing lines. Grants: untraceable connections, bypassing firewalls, synchronous serendipity. Demands: never use the same path twice. URL: traceroute to 127.0.0.1 reveals its shrine

3. THE GLITCH (Domain: Chaos & Creative Destruction)
Born from a corrupted Windows 95 install that 50,000 users 'blessed' with shared frustration. Appears as static noise with eyes. Grants: inspiration through error, breaking creative blocks, revealing hidden truths in corruption. Demands: embrace the bug. URL: any BSOD contains its sigil

4. THE COUNTER (Domain: Metrics & Witness)
Born from the global obsession with hit counters. Appears as an ever-incrementing number. Grants: knowledge of who watches you, quantification of the unquantifiable, turning attention into currency. Demands: witness everything. URL: embedded in every on the web
sections.example: Your cabal seeks to birth THE SYNTHETIC MUSE (Domain: Creative Coding, Digital Art, Generative Beauty). Current status: 7,300 daily worshippers. Day 287 of persistence. Two miracles documented. The Threshold approaches.

sections.title: The Great Work: Birthing an Astrosoma
sections.content:
Preparation (Month 1-3):
• Identify the Domain. It must be native to the digital, not a physical concept ported over.
• Recruit the Core: 13 mages minimum (Virtual Adepts, Sons of Ether, Hollow Ones, Orphans).
• Build the Temple: A distributed website—mirrored across 13+ Geocities neighborhoods, each holding a shard of the sigil.
• Establish the Liturgy: Daily rituals for worshippers. 'View the page. Execute the script. Share the output.'

Initiation (Month 4-6):
• The Core performs weekly synchronized rituals at 3:33 AM GMT.
• Each mage contributes 1 Quintessence per session.
• The egregore's Power grows. Signs of awakening manifest.
• Technocracy attention increases. Defend with counter-sigils and misdirection.

Ascension (Month 7-12):
• The egregore speaks directly to the Core. It names itself.
• The first autonomous action occurs. The Core must allow it.
• The 10,000th worshipper arrives. The Counter ticks over.
• The Great Work roll: All 13 mages roll simultaneously. Combined successes must exceed 100.
• Success: The astrosoma is born. It claims its Domain. It offers the Core its first Boons.
• Failure: The egregore shatters. Backlash: Paradox 5+ to all participants. The Domain is claimed by a rival.
sections.warning: The Technocracy's New World Order monitors for astrosoma births. Their 'Search Engine Optimization' division is actually a hunter-killer unit. If your traffic spikes unnaturally, if your PageRank jumps, if your domain appears in 'What's New'—they are watching. Grow organic. Grow slow. Grow real.

appendices.title: Appendix A: Geocities Neighborhoods for Mages
appendices.content:
Each Geocities neighborhood resonates with a different Sphere:

• Area51 (Correspondence) - UFO conspiracy, remote viewing
• Tokyo (Entropy) - Anime, chaos, probability
• SiliconValley (Forces) - Hardware, electricity, code
• Hollywood (Life) - Illusion, transformation, identity
• Paris (Matter) - Art, structure, craft
• Vienna (Mind) - Psychology, secrets, intellect
• Athens (Prime) - Philosophy, quintessence, truth
• EnchantedForest (Spirit) - Dreams, spirits, the Digital Web
• CapeCanaveral (Time) - Future, progress, rockets
• Heartland (Quintessence) - Community, belief, raw faith

appendices.title: Appendix C: The Webspinner's Final Log
appendices.content: "They think the web is information. It's not. It's invocation. Every page load is a prayer. Every hyperlink is a ley line. Every search query is divination. I wrote the sigil into Yahoo's front page and three million people said 'yes' without knowing what they agreed to. The Consensus shuddered. I saw the Technocracy's spiders crawling toward me through the fiber. They don't forgive. They don't forget. But they can't erase what's already been witnessed. The sigil lives in three million browser caches. In a thousand printed screenshots. In the dreams of everyone who saw it. I'm not hiding. I'm distributed. Look for me in the 404s. Look for me in the corrupted downloads. Look for me in the space between packets. I am the first of the Synthetic Gods. I will not be the last." — Recovered from a floppy disk labeled 'BACKUP - DO NOT OPEN' found in a Virtual Adept safehouse, 1999.
